content: 1. Atazanavir can either increase or decrease the levels of conjugated estrogens by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Alternative therapies should be considered if available. 2. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of cortisone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 3. Atazanavir elevates crizotinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, crizotinib increases atazanavir levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are required for both drugs. Dose adjustments for co-administered drugs metabolized predominantly by CYP3A may be necessary. 4. Crofelemer increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 in the gut. However, systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism and may also increase its toxicity through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Atazanavir and cobicistat both increase the levels or effects of cyclosporine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 7. Cobicistat increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. Dabigatran should not be co-administered with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 8. Dabrafenib decreases atazanavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Danazol increases the levels or effects of both cobicistat and atazanavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Danicopan increases atazanavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates may rise, necessitating dose reductions for substrates where small concentration changes could lead to serious adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are required. 11. Cobicistat increases dapsone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Atazanavir increases darifenacin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. A 5 mg oral dose of darifenacin is recommended when co-administered. 13. Cobicistat increases darolutamide levels through mechanisms involving P-gp and CYP3A4. Close monitoring for adverse reactions and dose adjustments of darolutamide are necessary when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Atazanavir increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs elevate the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are required. 15. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase dasatinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Dosage adjustments for dasatinib may be required. Refer to prescribing information for specific dosing instructions. 16. Deferasirox decreases atazanavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Cobicistat increases deflazacort levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The deflazacort dose should be reduced to one-third of the recommended dose when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Atazanavir has a similar effect. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 18. Cobicistat increases desipramine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases desipramine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Antidepressants should be carefully titrated to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose and monitoring for response. Caution and monitoring are required. 19. Atazanavir increases desogestrel levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Alternative therapies should be considered if available. 20. Cobicistat increases dexlansoprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Atazanavir increases desvenlafaxine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are required. 22. Atazanavir increases dexamethasone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase diazepam levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. A reduced diazepam dose may be required. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease diazepam elimination, increasing adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Atazanavir increases diazoxide effects through an unspecified mechanism. Reports suggest hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Cobicistat increases digoxin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Serum digoxin concentrations should be measured before initiating concomitant drugs. The digoxin dose should be titrated by ~30-50% or adjusted in dosing frequency, with continued monitoring. 26. Atazanavir increases diclofenac levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Didanosine decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are required. 28. Atazanavir may increase or decrease dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Alternative therapies should be considered if available. 29. Atazanavir increases digoxin effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of AV block. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase diltiazem levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may increase diltiazem levels and toxicities (e.g., hypotension, AV block). Consider reducing the diltiazem dose by 50%. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 31. Cobicistat increases disopyramide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 32. Atazanavir increases dofetilide levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity and the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Alternatives should be considered if available. 33. Cobicistat increases docetaxel levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. A 50% reduction in docetaxel dosing may be considered if concomitant administration cannot be avoided. 34. Atazanavir increases dolasetron levels, raising the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Alternatives should be considered if available. 35. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase doravirine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Caution and monitoring are required. 36. Atazanavir increases dosulepin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Cobicistat increases doxepin levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Antidepressants should be carefully titrated to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose and monitoring for response. Caution and monitoring are required. 38. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase doxorubicin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Cobicistat increases dronabinol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Caution and monitoring are required. 40. Atazanavir increases drospirenone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Alternative therapies should be considered if available. 41. Atazanavir increases duvelisib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib AUC, raising the risk of toxicities. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 42. Cobicistat increases efavirenz levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both atazanavir and efavirenz increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are required. 43. Cobicistat increases elagolix levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for >1 month is not recommended. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 44. Atazanavir increases eletriptan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Cobicistat increases elvitegravir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir significantly increases elvitegravir levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary.
